articles.title: Macklemore cut from Ed Sheeran U.S. tour after onstage 'Free Palestine' remarks
articles.summary: Macklemore has been dropped from the remainder of Ed Sheeran's tour, according to the Rolling Stone, after several venues in the United States said they would not allow the concerts to be held if the…

image.caption: U.S. rapper, singer, dancer and DJ Benjamin Haggerty, known as Macklemore, performs in central-eastern France on Aug. 30. The Seattle rapper was cut from the remainder of Ed Sheeran's U.S. leg tour, Macklemore said in a statement, after billionaire Robert Kraft said he would not be allowed to perfor

blocks.text: Entertainment

Macklemore has been dropped from the remainder of Ed Sheeran's tour, according to the Rolling Stone, after several venues in the United States said they would not allow the concerts to be held if the American rapper, who is an outspoken Palestinian advocate, remains on the lineup.
U.S. rapper blames NFL owner, says Sheeran told him 'Free Palestine' chant was 'hurtful' to many

Macklemore has been dropped from the U.S. leg of English singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran's tour after several venues in the United States threatened to cancel the scheduled concerts if the American rapper — and outspoken advocate for Palestinians — was not removed.

Benjamin Hammond Haggerty, better known by his stage name Macklemore, joined Sheeran for the first two U.S. shows on the Loop Tour on Sept. 4 and 5 at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. The Seattle-born Grammy winner was slated to open for the remaining eight of Sheeran's 10 U.S. shows before he was dropped from the tour.

Macklemore's onstage remarks at MetLife — including chanting "Free Palestine" and expressing solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza and the Israeli-occupied West Bank — drew some controversy from pro-Israel groups. The rapper also wore a keffiyeh, a checkered black-and-white scarf long worn by Palestinians, and performed his song Hind's Hall, one of two songs he released in 2024 in support of student protesters on university campuses and to decry Israel's military actions in Gaza following Oct. 7, 2023.

The Israeli American Council (IAC) also launched a petition calling for Sheeran to remove Macklemore from the rest of the tour. In a statement issued following the announcement he would be cut, the IAC said it welcomes the decision.

"Anyone who chooses to turn an 80,000-person concert into a vehicle for advancing a one-sided political agenda must stand behind that choice," it said. "A concert stage is not a platform for anti-Israel and antisemitic propaganda."
Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of the tour, told Rolling Stone magazine that the decision to remove Macklemore came after "discussions with stakeholders."

"As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran's U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," the group said on Monday.

Macklemore responded Monday in a lengthy statement posted on Instagram, blaming his removal from the tour on New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who he claimed rallied other stadium owners to threaten to cancel scheduled concerts if Macklemore was not taken off the bill. The rapper said the threat to cancel the tour dates placed Sheeran, his friend, in a difficult position after Kraft, who also owns Gillette Stadium, said Macklemore would not be allowed onstage.

"Ed [Sheeran] was in a f--ked up position. He knew it. His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before. He told me that the words 'Free Palestine' and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with," Macklemore said.

"I told him that if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood. But he couldn't get past his public facing, 'I don't take sides.'"
CBC News reached out to representatives for Sheeran for comment but did not immediately hear back.
Kraft responds to Macklemore

In response to Macklemore, Kraft said Gillette Stadium does "not provide a platform for hate speech," accusing the rapper of divisiveness and hate by sharing "selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas," in a statement shared with CBC News.

"Based on Macklemore's recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran's shows in New Jersey and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line," Kraft said in an email.
"I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same – peace for all people, an end to suffering and an end to all hate.”

In his onstage speech at the first show, Macklemore said: "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine.
"I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them."
Macklemore added that his criticism was directed at Israel's government and was not an attack on Jewish people.

"To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters: criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you," he said in his speech onstage at the second show on Sept. 5. "My message is for peace; love for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect and equality."

Following his comments, singer-songwriter Pink reshared a social media post from StopAntisemitism calling for him to be removed from the tour. She later said that the post "said things in words I didn't write, and I wouldn't have chosen all of them," but defended her criticism of the rapper.

"He stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn't about them. You don't get to decide that for us," Pink said on Friday in a lengthy statement on Instagram.

items: More musicians are speaking out about Gaza than ever before. Why now?
Gaza doc NAZA earns 24.5-minute standing ovation at Venice premiere

blocks.text: "That's what prompted my repost. Not 'Free Palestine,' and not anyone's right to say it. I have never asked for another artist to be silenced and I'm not asking now," she wrote.

Pink also recalled a 2014 performance by Macklemore in which he wore a costume onstage that was widely criticized as offensive and antisemitic. The rapper later apologized, saying, "I respect all cultures and all people," and that the costume was not meant to be a caricature of a Jewish man.
Humanitarian groups have said Israel's actions constitute genocide
Reaction to Macklemore's statement on Monday included support for the rapper.

"The way you stand in solidarity here is an absolute model. Thank you for walking through this fire while centering Palestinians," commented Noura Erakat, a Palestinian-American activist, professor and human rights attorney.

"Thank you for recognizing your relative power and privilege. Thank you for having the humility to be changed by Palestinians, enough to learn not just a phrase but a pillar of our continuity — thank you for not abandoning this duty."
U.S. singer-songwriter Lauren Jauregui, who has also been an advocate for Palestinians, said: "So much love and respect for you."

items: Hannah Einbinder, Ilana Glazer and other Hollywood stars defend Mark Ruffalo against antisemitism accusations

blocks.text: Popular children's content creator Rachel Accurso, known as Ms. Rachel, has similarly faced intense public reaction and antisemitism accusations for using her platform to highlight the humanitarian needs, safety and rights of children in Gaza.

"Ed Sheeran had an opportunity [to] show that we won't be bullied into punishing people for supporting Palestine," she wrote on Instagram. "Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows. A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak out against it."
Humanitarian organizations including Amnesty International and a United Nations commission have said Israel's actions in Gaza constitute a genocide.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Sara Jabakhanji is a Toronto-based senior writer assigned to cover news developments in the Middle East. She has worked in CBC bureaus in Ottawa, London and Toronto. You can reach her at sara.jabakhanji@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Europe must build own AI or risk getting cut off by US or China, says ECB’s Lagarde
articles.summary:
Central bank chief says continent’s AI dependency could give trade partners unprecedented leverage in negotiations

Europe must develop its own AI technology and build more datacentres in…

blocks.text: Europe must develop its own AI technology and build more datacentres in order to nullify the threat of being cut off by the US or China, according to the president of the European Central Bank.

Christine Lagarde said the continent needed AI models – the technology that powers AI tools such as chatbots – that were “good enough” to carry out most tasks and run from domestic datacentres. If Europe invests in its own AI tech, said Lagarde, “the threat of being cut off loses its force”.

AI is being built elsewhere, the ECB boss said in a speech in Vienna, with the US producing 59 notable models last year and China 35, while France and the UK produced one each. She added that the US hosts 75% of the world’s AI computing capacity – produced by datacentres – and Europe just 5%.

Lagarde said Europe faced “an awkward choice”. “Either it holds back on adopting, because it cannot protect its data, and forgoes the growth. Or it adopts AI quickly, becomes highly dependent, and risks losing the freedom to organise its economy according to its own values.”
Cutting Europe off from AI or changing the terms of its access would have a widespread and immediate economic impact, she said.

blocks.caption: Datacentre run by French company OVHcloud in Roubaix – Lagarde wants Europe to have more domestic capacity. Photograph: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: “Within a few years it will be screening goods at the border, deciding which tax returns are audited, dispatching trains, watching patients on wards and clearing payments at banks. A withdrawal of access, or a change in its terms, would then reach every sector at once,” she said.
Lagarde said this represented leverage that “no trade partner has ever held over Europe, and it could be ‌used in any negotiation, on tariffs or on digital taxes, for example”.

While the EU and the US remain key allies, the Trump administration has shaken that trust in a range of episodes including the imposition of tariffs, demands to take over Greenland – a largely autonomous territory that is part of the Danish commonwealth – and the withdrawal of US troops from Europe over political disagreements.

blocks.caption: Donald Trump, pictured at an event in the White House last year, has shaken trust with his new tariff regime. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: If adopted quickly, AI could lift the level of productivity – a measure of economic performance – by up to 4% over a decade, which would be ​transformative for public finances, Lagarde said.

Urging Europe to build more computing capacity, she said: “Europe already has too little datacentre capacity to meet its own demand, and on current trends, that gap is projected to grow more than sixfold within a decade.”

US ​technology firms’ investment ‌needs are so ​large that they are ​doing some of their borrowing in Europe, pushing up costs for everyone else as they crowd out others in the debt market. European pension funds also invest heavily in US tech stocks, so any market correction would affect European savings, she added.
Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: 2 more people have died exploring Banff National Park, police say
articles.summary: A 24-year-old climber died after a significant fall from Recondite Peak in Banff National Park on Wednesday, while a 33-year-old hiker died on Saturday near Devil's Thumb and the Big Beehive area by…

image.caption: The entry sign for Banff National Park at the east gates. The park has seen multiple deaths this summer. (Greg Colgan/CBC)

blocks.text: Calgary·New

A 24-year-old climber died after a significant fall from Recondite Peak in Banff National Park on Wednesday, while a 33-year-old hiker died on Saturday near Devil's Thumb and the Big Beehive area by Lake Louise, according to police.
7 hiking, climbing-related deaths in Banff, Kananaskis this summer
Two people died in Banff National Park in the last week while exploring the outdoors, police say.

A 24-year-old climber died after a significant fall from Recondite Peak in Banff National Park on Wednesday, while a 33-year-old hiker died on Saturday near Devil's Thumb and the Big Beehive area by Lake Louise, said local RCMP detachment commander Susan Richter.

Richter said the climber had hiked into the remote area on Sept. 7 to ascend Recondite Peak and was in contact with people via a communication device. They reported him missing on Sept. 9, and police said Parks Canada rescue specialists found him dead the same day.
Richter said he was on his own, but "very trained and experienced in the back country."

Recondite Peak is in the eastern part of Banff National Park and roughly 3,350 metres high. The area is north of Lake Louise and to the east of the Icefields Parkway. It sits along the provincial border at the Siffleur Wilderness Area.
Parks Canada's Banff field unit didn't respond to CBC's request for information and an interview.
Second death near Lake Louise
On Saturday afternoon, a 33-year-old Calgary man was hiking with three friends near Devil's Thumb and the Big Beehive close to Lake Louise, said police.
He went on his own to Devil's Thumb. When his friends lost sight of him, Richter said they reported him missing. Parks Canada rescue specialists were sent out, and confirmed the man had died.
Parks Canada's Lake Louise, Yoho and Kootenay field unit is working to get additional details.
A grim summer

Banff National Park and Kananaskis Country have had five other hiking-related deaths this summer combined. A 47-year-old woman died hiking Mount Bryant in June, while a 65-year-old man died on Mount Temple in July, and a woman in her twenties died falling from Marvel Peak that same month.
In August, a woman died on Mount Yamnuska, and a female hiker died on Tent Ridge.

There have also been three drownings in the Bow Valley in the past few months: a 25-year-old American man at Johnston Canyon, a 29-year-old Banff resident at Johnson Lake and a 33-year-old man at Quarry Lake in Canmore.

Richter said regardless of skill level, all people should plan ahead, know the trail and know their abilities when recreating outdoors. She said it's safer to travel in a group and stick to "well used trails with higher visibility."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Greg Colgan is a journalist for CBC in the Bow Valley. He was previously the editor of the Rocky Mountain Outlook in Banff and Canmore. He has also worked for media outlets in Ontario and has experience covering topics such as sports, politics, housing and development, courts and arts and entertainment. He joined CBC in 2025. He can be reached at greg.colgan@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
articles.summary: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing, Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners"…

image.caption: Ukraine has been targeting Russian oil refinieries with long range drones this year, while Russia's strategy of firing on Ukrainian power infrastructure is well establishedImage: Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump claimed a breakthrough on Monday in diplomacy between Ukraine and Russia, although his unsubstantiated declaration only elicited a very reserved comment from Ukraine and no immediate word from the Kremlin.
The assertion comes amid indications from both Russia and Ukraine that they would be willing to continue with US-brokere mediations, which have been largely stagnant throughout Trump's second term.

Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy last week told DW that he would be willing to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the G20 summit in Miami in December if rumors of Putin being invited materilialized.
What did Trump say?
Trump appeared to claim that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to stop hitting each other's energy targets.
"Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!" Trump or his team wrote.

"The World's Diesel price is mostly caused by the Russia/Ukraine War [sic], not Iran," the Truth Social comment continued, demonstrating — as a quickfire series of agitated follow-up posts would reinforce — a desire to downplay rising US oil prices, the role of Trump's war in Iran in pushing them skywards, and economic pressures closer to home.
Donald Trump blames Ukraine for record US diesel prices
What, if anything, did Ukraine and Russia say?
There was no immediate comment on the matter from Moscow.
Ukraine's presidency declined to comment but President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued a more guarded statement online.
He did, however, say that he had recommended seeking such an accord, as winter approaches — if Russia's cooperation could be ensured after years of it targeting Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

"Ukraine has proposed that its partners secure an agreement with Russia that would stop the destruction of critical infrastructure," Zelenskyy wrote online. "Food, energy, and other basics that sustain life must be protected, and Russian strikes are directed primarily against them."
But Zelenskyy cautioned that Kyiv "is not convinced that Russia is willing to abide by an agreement," if one could be reached.

"If our partners are ready to ensure that Russia genuinely refrains from striking our electricity system, other energy facilities, critical infrastructure, and food supply routes, then, of course, we are ready to ensure a corresponding halt to our strikes."
He said Kyiv would need assurance that this was a lasting deal and not just a bid to secure temporary relief in fuel prices in Russia ahead of elections at the end of the week.
"We expect specifics from our partners," Zelenskyy concluded, without naming names.
Ukraine has been targeting Russian warehouses, refineries amid Iran war

As Trump's war in Iran pushed oil prices to highs not seen since the immediate aftermath of Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Kyiv has started using long-range drone strikes to target Russia's refinery and petroleum supply infrastructure.
This has caused isolated shortages and price increases, even in oil-rich Russia.
Ukraine has also launched a series of high-profile strikes on Russia's best-known online retailer Wildberries, accusing it of providing logistical support to the military.

The US miltiary action of the last six months in the Gulf has also left Ukraine poorly placed to defend itself against Russian ballistic missiles, because of US Patriot missile supplies being depleted in the Middle East.

In recent winters, Russia has frequently targeted Ukraine's energy infrastructure to try to exacerbate difficulties of dealing with the cold. Last winter, as a particularly fierce cold snap hit Kyiv and other parts of the country, Trump announced a brief halt to strikes on Kyiv which only held for a few days.

articles.title: Andrew Davies admits to drawing on ‘stimulating’ Made in Chelsea for Jane Austen adaptation
articles.summary:
Screenwriter points to parallels between two worlds while academic says some of author’s characters ‘would make perfect reality show contestants’

If Jane Austen’s novels run on closed social…
articles.byline: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent

blocks.text: If Jane Austen’s novels run on closed social worlds, courtship rituals, status anxiety, gossip and relentless scrutiny of who’s coupling with who, it follows that the obvious contemporary equivalent would be reality television.
That’s according to Andrew Davies, the writer who has spent decades modernising British period dramas.
Speaking on Radio 4’s Today programme on Monday, Davies revealed that he had been watching Made in Chelsea while working on an adaptation of Austen’s unfinished novel The Watsons.

“It’s stimulating really for relationships and ideas,” he said of the Channel 4 series, which follows the relationship dramas and social rivalries of affluent young residents of west London. “These young men and women in The Watsons, for example, are very analogous to Made in Chelsea.”

blocks.caption: Andrew Davies said the young men and women in The Watsons were ‘very analogous’ to the characters of the Made in Chelsea reality show. Photograph: David Sillitoe/The Guardian

blocks.text: Davies, whose memoir An Unsuitable Boy: A Life in Scripts is out this week, is responsible for the legendary image of Colin Firth as Mr Darcy emerging from a lake in a wet shirt in his 1995 BBC adaptation of Pride and Prejudice, which went some way to injecting Austen into Bridget Jones, written by Helen Fielding around the time it aired. His approach, he said, had been about “bringing out the sex that’s inherent in Austen”.

He has previously described his 2019 adaptation of Sanditon as “Love Island” in Austen’s world and talked about whether Charlotte would “friend-zone” someone or experience a “fanny flutter”. Meanwhile Rose Williams, who starred in the series, said she believed “Austen would probably write something satirical about Love Island if she were alive today”.

Joe Bray, an Austen scholar and professor of English at the University of Sheffield, said of the author: “Jane Austen was a shrewd observer of the fashionable manners and fads adopted by the young … and the plots of most of her novels are driven by sexual attraction and/or secret liaisons and engagements.”
The Steele sisters in Sense and Sensibility, he suggested, “would make perfect reality show contestants”.

Austen also pioneered a way of representing the unspoken thoughts and feelings of her female characters that can be difficult to translate to screen. But Bray noted that Austen herself loved gossiping about neighbours and acquaintances in letters to her sister Cassandra. “I can’t say for certain whether or not she would be a viewer of Made in Chelsea or Love Island,” he said, “but … she would be interested at least!”

An academic essay on Made in Chelsea described the programme as a “kind of homage” to Austen, arguing that its subject was the “courtship rituals” of young people with money and property, and compared its social world to Pride and Prejudice and Emma.

blocks.caption: Austen scholar Joe Bray suggested that the author would have at least been interested in the likes of Made in Chelsea and Love Island. Photograph: Stock Montage/Getty Images

blocks.text: There is indeed a human link between Made in Chelsea and Netflix’s forthcoming Pride and Prejudice: the latter’s writer and executive producer, Dolly Alderton, began her career as a story producer on the reality show – where, she has said, her job involved turning the romantic entanglements of wealthy young Londoners into “a four-part comedy drama”.

It remains to be seen whether the Netflix series draws any inspiration from Made in Chelsea, but Reddit users have previously theorised about whether Alderton took inspiration from the reality show, or her TV adaptation of her memoir Everything I Know About Love. “Who do we think the character ‘Kyle’ is based off? I’m getting Spencer Matthews and Jamie Laing [both Made in Chelsea cast members],” one wrote.

In her 2016 modernisation of Pride and Prejudice, Eligible, novelist Curtis Sittenfeld’s transplanted the Bennets to contemporary Cincinnati and made Chip Bingley a former reality-TV star who had appeared on The Bachelor.

“Reality dating shows are so formulaic, and courtship in Austen’s time was rigid and proscriptive,” Sittenfeld said. In other words, reality TV provided a modern equivalent for Austen’s world of carefully prescribed romantic encounters; in place of the wealthy unmarried man arriving in the neighbourhood, there is the reality-TV bachelor whose romantic availability is already a matter of public interest.

That may explain the extraordinary portability of Austen, from Clueless, which transplanted Emma to 1990s LA, and Bridget Jones’s Diary to Fire Island, Persuasion and the forthcoming Sense and Sensibility.
John Mullan, a literature professor at University College London and historical and dialogue consultant on Bridgerton, identified another parallel.
“In Austen’s fiction, courtship mostly takes place under the eyes of others,” he said. “Young women and men who might fancy each other are very rarely alone.”
But, he added, there is a crucial difference: “What about propriety, restraint, repression? These are also key to Austen’s stories and characters.”

articles.title: 64% of Filipinos say congressmen doing 'good job' -- OCTA
articles.summary: At least 64% of Filipinos say that the their district representative is "doing a good job" in the House of Representatives, according to OCTA Research.

blocks.text: Published September 15, 2026 1:39am
At least 64% of Filipinos say that the their district representative is "doing a good job" in the House of Representatives, according to OCTA Research.
Meanwhile, 27% disagree, while 9% say they do not know or cannot say. No respondents refused to answer the question.

Based on its second quarter Tugon ng Masa survey released on Monday, the 64% positive assessment of local district representatives is notably higher than the 38% trust rating and 37% positive performance rating recorded for the House of Representatives as an institution.

The result, the research stated, "suggests that accountability in Philippine politics may operate more effectively, or at least more visibly, at the constituency level than at the level of the institution itself."

"This has implications beyond public opinion measurement: it bears on how legislators themselves may calculate political incentives, since a representative's standing with constituents appears largely decoupled from the public's broader assessment of Congress. It also offers a partial explanation for a familiar pattern in Philippine electoral behavior — the persistence of high incumbent reelection rates in individual districts alongside persistently low institutional trust in Congress as a whole."
The survey was conducted from July 4 to 11, 2026 through face-to-face interviews among 1,200 respondents, aged 18 and above with a ±3 percent margin of error and 95 percent confidence level.
Geography, socioeconomic class, age group
The Visayas records the highest level of agreement at 68%, followed by Mindanao at 65%, Balance Luzon at 63%, and the National Capital Region at 60%.

And by socioeconomic class, positive assessments are highest among Class E at 72%, compared with 63% among Class D and 62% among Class ABC. Disagreement ranges from 25% to 30% across the major areas and from 25% to 28% across socioeconomic classes.
The survey showed that across age groups, satisfaction is highest among respondents aged 65 to 74 at 72%, followed by those aged 18 to 24 at 66% and those aged 35 to 44 at 65%.

Agreement is lowest among respondents aged 25 to 34 and those aged 75 and above, both at 60%. Respondents aged 75 and above also record the largest proportion who say they do not know or cannot say, at 18%.
On place and gender, 65% of rural respondents and 63% of urban respondents agree that their district representative is doing a good job while agreement stands at 64% among both males and females.

By educational attainment, satisfaction is highest among respondents with no formal or elementary education at 67%, followed by high school and college or postgraduate respondents, both at 64%. Respondents with vocational education record the lowest level of agreement at 58% and the highest level of disagreement at 35%. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Bolsonaro 2.0: Brazil braces for the return of the far right
articles.summary:
With Lula mired in scandal, Flávio Bolsonaro is firing up his base in the bellwether state of Minas Gerais – starting at the scene of his father’s stabbing

A giant banner of Brazil’s…
articles.byline: Tom Phillips in Juiz de Fora

blocks.text: A giant banner of Brazil’s incarcerated former president Jair Bolsonaro fluttered in the morning breeze as his eldest son, Flávio, touched down at an airfield on the fringe of a city that will soon help decide the future of one of the biggest democracies on earth.

“Brazil is rudderless. Brazil has no president and Brazil needs a president – and that president is Flávio Bolsonaro,” the far-right senator declared as he waded into the flock of supporters who had gathered to welcome him to Juiz de Fora, one of the largest cities in the battleground state of Minas Gerais.

With less than a month before nearly 159 million Brazilians choose their next leader on 4 October, the election appears on a knife-edge, with the incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and his challenger, Flávio Bolsonaro, neck-and-neck in the polls.

blocks.caption: Bolsonaro supporters float a giant balloon depicting the US president, Donald Trump, holding Brazil’s president, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Photograph: Miguel Schincariol/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Bolsonaro’s campaign appears to have seized the momentum in recent weeks amid a slew of corruption scandals involving Lula’s son and the supreme court. That has prompted despair among progressives who fear their country could fall back into the hands of a radical rightwing movement that tried to grab power after the then-president, Jair Bolsonaro, lost the 2022 election to Lula.

Last September, Jair Bolsonaro received a 27-year jail sentence for spearheading that botched coup – a verdict supporters insist was unjust. But the ex-president and his accomplices are likely to be freed if his son wins power – a prospect that delights the hardcore Bolsonaristas who turned out to greet Flávio Bolsonaro wearing yellow football shirts and headbands reading: “Lula out!”

“Today is a moment of joy,” said Ulisses Lima, 50, a cybersecurity specialist with a Jesus Christ pendant around his neck. “Flávio represents change. He represents Brazil’s rescue from this socialist abyss we’ve spent so long warning about,” Lima added as supporters waited for the former president’s heir to arrive.

blocks.caption: Brazil’s president Lula at a reelection campaign rally in Curitiba on Saturday. Photograph: Rodolfo Bührer/Reuters

blocks.text: Nearby, another devotee, José Caldeira, fell to his knees and begged for divine intervention to get Bolsonaro out of house arrest. “God, free this nation! Amnesty and freedom for Bolsonaro!” Caldeira bellowed, raising his hands towards the sky.

A third man, Davi Frederico, held a banner celebrating Donald Trump, who has been accused of trying to swing the election in Bolsonaro’s favour through economic and diplomatic pressure. “Make Liberals Cry Again,” it said.

Juiz de Fora, an industrial and university city traditionally associated with the left, is also a key location for Brazil’s hard right. The city’s army headquarters was the launchpad for the 1964 coup that plunged Brazil into two decades of military rule. And it was in Juiz de Fora, on the eve of the 2018 election, that Jair Bolsonaro was stabbed in the gut while campaigning – an attack widely believed to have helped the former paratrooper seal his victory.

blocks.caption: Davi Frederico at the airport in Juiz de Fora. Photograph: Alan Lima/The Guardian

blocks.text: Bolsonaro’s shock win ushered in what, from a progressive perspective, were four abysmal years. Destruction of the Amazon rainforest and gun ownership skyrocketed, hundreds of thousands died during a Covid outbreak Bolsonaro was accused of mishandling, and the president’s authoritarian rhetoric and attacks on Brazil’s electronic voting system culminated in the 8 January 2023 riots in Brasília. The supreme court later called those disturbances part of a plot to “annihilate” the country’s democracy.
But the Bolsonaros still enjoy abundant support, and that devotion was visible as Flávio Bolsonaro’s motorcade crept towards the high street where his father was ambushed eight years ago.

blocks.caption: Street hawkers at Flavio Bolsonaro’s campaign event pay tribute to the US connection. Photograph: Alan Lima/The Guardian

blocks.text: “Let’s get the left out! Let’s get these motherfuckers out!” one elderly woman shrieked as the senator passed by on top of a sound truck stamped with the word: “Jesus”. Other fans, many senior citizens, waved Brazil flags from windows or stood on the sidewalk flashing victory signs with their hands.

“Barring some kind of leftwing trickery, Flávio Bolsonaro can already be considered president. All you have to do is take a look at the streets and social media,” claimed Nikolas Ferreira, an influential far-right congressman from Minas Gerais who has more than 9 million TikTok followers.

Alongside the enthusiasm, there were glimpses of the revulsion many Brazilians feel for the former president. One leftwinger took to his balcony with a loudhailer to taunt the Bolsonaristas as they paraded through town. “Trump! Trump! Get my daddy out of jail!” the dissenter jeered in reference to the US president’s attempts to help Bolsonaro escape punishment.

blocks.caption: Supporters gather to greet Flávio Bolsonaro at Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais. Photograph: Alan Lima/The Guardian

blocks.text: Minas Gerais, a mountainous mining and agricultural region that is larger than France and has 21 million inhabitants, is Brazil’s bellwether state. Since democracy returned in the 1980s, no candidate has won the presidency without triumphing here. In 2018, Jair Bolsonaro beat Lula’s candidate in Minas by more than 1.7m votes. Four years later, Lula reclaimed the state by fewer than 50,000. After landing in Minas last week, Flávio Bolsonaro said he was confident of clawing back the swing state, with one recent poll putting him ahead there.

“[Lula] is a president who you look at and see the past,” the 45-year-old senator said of his 80-year-old adversary. “With Flávio you can be sure that when people look at him, they see a modern government and a government of the future.”

Thomas Traumann, a political analyst who has written a book about his polarised country, said the election was too close to call. “It’s a coin flip,” said Traumann, who believed an unexpected scandal or last-minute “black swan” event could swing the election either way. On Friday, it emerged that Flávio Bolsonaro had been placed under police investigation over suspicions of corruption involving the funding of a big-budget biopic telling the story of the assassination attempt against his father in Juiz de Fora.

blocks.caption: Flávio Bolsonaro addresses supporters at the spot where Jair Bolsonaro was stabbed in Juiz de Fora during the 2018 presidential campaign. Photograph: Pablo Porciúncula/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: For progressive voters, the vision for a Flávio Bolsonaro administration laid out during his visit to Minas is the stuff of nightmares. “I think Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidency is going to be Jair Bolsonaro 2.0,” said Bruno Engler, a Bolsonarista lawmaker from Minas’ capital, Belo Horizonte.

Engler believed a top priority would be zero-tolerance policing, with the younger Bolsonaro pledging an iron-fisted crackdown on criminals his father has compared to cockroaches. “Thugs who don’t surrender will be arrested or neutralised,” Engler vowed, predicting gun laws would be loosened.

Speaking on the street corner where his father was knifed, Flávio Bolsonaro vowed to pack Brazil’s 11-member supreme court with five conservative judges “who are against abortion [and] against drugs”. “We’re going to give the streets back to the Brazilian people … We’re going to lower the age of criminal responsibility. We are going to introduce chemical castration for rapists,” shouted the candidate, who wore a bullet-proof vest.

Those pledges prompted whoops of excitement from the crush of supporters below Bolsonaro’s truck. Dozens ofmobile phones captured the candidate’s every word. But amid the rightwing rejoicing there was fear and trepidation, too.

blocks.caption: Lennon César: ‘Brazilians have short memories when it comes to the past.’  Photograph: Alan Lima/The Guardian

blocks.text: Lennon César, a law student and leftwing activist who had come to confront Bolsonaro’s fans, voiced incredulity that less than four years after Jair Bolsonaro’s failed power grab, tens of millions of Brazilians seemed poised to vote for his son.

“We were the victims of an attempted coup – and his father was the perpetrator,” recalled César, 28. “It’s terrifying. And the thing that worries me most is that the general public doesn’t really seem to get what’s happening. Brazilians have short memories when it comes to the past.”
As a black, gay man, César felt particular dread at the prospect of a second Bolsonaro presidency, given the patriarch’s hostility to minorities.

César vowed to vote for Lula, Brazil’s first working-class president, calling him the only leader who paid attention to the poor. “If today I’m studying for a law degree it’s because one of Lula’s government programmes allowed me to achieve that,” he said, warning: “These people … might destroy it all.”
A few blocks away, a graffiti artist had spray painted their own message of disapproval on to the facade of Bolsonaro’s Juiz de Fora HQ. “Facists [sic],” it read.

blocks.caption: Graffiti on Flávio Bolsonaro’s headquarters in the city of Juiz de Fora. Photograph: Alan Lima/The Guardian

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney's 'sexualized' sports betting ad slammed by female athletes
articles.summary: U.S. actor Sydney Sweeney is once again facing backlash over an advertisement. But this time, she's enraged female athletes around the world with a nude sports betting ad — and her response.

image.caption: A composite image of screen grabs of social media posts from athletes Canadian Sophia Jensen, left, Canadian Madeline Schizas, centre, and American Gracie Kramer, posted over the Sept. 12-13 weekend in response to a new sports betting ad featuring U.S. actor Sydney Sweeney. (@sophiajensenCA/TikTok,

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
U.S. actor Sydney Sweeney is once again facing backlash over an advertisement. But this time, she's enraged female athletes around the world with a nude sports betting ad — and her response.
Canadian skier, canoeist, skater among athletes criticizing Novig ad
U.S. actor Sydney Sweeney is once again facing backlash over an advertisement.
This time, she has enraged female athletes around the world with a nude sports gambling ad — and her response.

The Novig sports prediction ad, posted online Sept. 9 and viewed nearly 39 million times by Monday morning, features Sweeney holding various pieces of sports equipment in front of what looks like her otherwise naked body, as bass music plays in the background.
"Think you know sports? Prove it," says the star of Euphoria and The Housemaid at the beginning of the ad as she holds a football in front of each breast.

In other shots, she perches on a basketball net while spinning a ball with only her hair covering her, holds a football in front of her pelvis, lies nude on a bench with a soccer ball resting on her feet and swings a golf club wearing only white underwear.

It set off a backlash from female athletes and Olympians who say the ad sexualizes women in sport and sets them back. The criticism crosses borders and a range of sports, with many posting "Dear Sydney Sweeney" videos on social media in response.

"Dear Sydney Sweeney, this is women in sports," Canadian sprint canoeist Sophia Jensen posted on TikTok on Sunday, alongside a video where the world champion competes on the water and trains in the gym.
"Hey Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," Canadian figure skater Madeline Schizas posted on Instagram with a similar video where she competes and trains on and off the ice.
"IDK what Sydney Sweeney was doing, but this is what a woman in sport looks like," posted U.S. gymnast Gracie Kramer over a similar montage.
British sprinter Amy Hunt got a word in during a post-race interview on Sunday, after she finished fourth in the 200-metre final at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest.
"Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," Hunt told BBC Sport, adding "hard work, blood, sweat, tears."
Australian swimmer Ariarne Titmus, the reigning Olympic champion in the 400-metre freestyle, called the ad "a kick in the face" on Instagram.
"How do we live in a world where monetizing a woman's body and sexualizing women's sport is still a thing?" she said, according to Australia's ABC News.

items: Spain's soccer federation will fund egg freezing. Is this a win for female athletes?
Women's sports are having a moment, but sexism is still holding back success

blocks.text: Novig CEO and co-founder Jacob Fortinsky praised the brand campaign for highlighting a platform that's "singularly focused on sports."
"Sydney helped bring that message to life in a way that’s impossible to ignore," Fortinsky said in a press release the same day the ad launched.
In the same press release, Sweeney called the campaign "a fun idea" that "brings that idea to life with confidence, humor and a playful edge."
Not her 1st controversial ad
If this is sounding familiar, Sweeney faced similar backlash last year over an American Eagle advertisement that was criticized for promoting white standards of beauty at best, and eugenics at worst.
In the ad, Sweeney makes a play on words between jeans (the clothing item) and genes (the genetic material).
“Genes are passed down from parents to offspring, often determining traits like hair colour, personality and even eye colour. My jeans are blue,” Sweeney said in the ad.
Some internet commentators read the ad as having eugenicist undertones. Eugenics is a discredited idea that the human race could be improved by selectively breeding for certain traits.

items: 'That’s not storytelling': Olympians hope proposed guidelines eliminate sexualization on broadcasts
Sydney Sweeney says she put her phone away during the American Eagle jeans ad controversy

blocks.text: At the time, the blond-haired, blue-eyed actor stood by the ad and downplayed the reaction, which included support from U.S. President Donald Trump, who called it the "HOTTEST ad out there."

Sweeney appeared to take a more overt approach to the backlash against her new ad, posting a series of photos on Instagram on Sunday that showed magazine covers with male and female athletes posing in little to no clothing.
What Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle ad says about the brand's marketing | Hanomansing Tonight
This move prompted even more backlash. Canadian alpine skier Cassidy Gray called it "idiotic" and "senseless."

"It's not a joke when your life is actually you being a female athlete, and you being sexualized or not taken seriously and not given the same opportunities, and then you see one of the most famous actresses in the world going and completely wiping away all the work that you have done to be taken seriously," Gray posted in an emotional video on TikTok.
Gray also responded to those who might say it's just a commercial and not meant to be taken so seriously.
"I fear you're just out of touch, because it really is that deep."
Female athletes have historically been marketed in an over-sexualized manner, with a greater focus on their appearance than their skills.

This also extends to sports coverage, with women at the Tokyo 2021 Olympics 10 times more likely to be "visually objectified" with a camera angle than men, according to a report from The Representation Project. Researchers defined visual objectification as when a camera panned across an athlete's body or focused on a specific body part in a sexualizing way.
The same study found female athletes were more likely to be infantilized by commentators, often called "young ladies" and "girls."

Another recent study from World Athletics found that female athletes were consistently targeted by online abuse more than their male counterparts at four global sporting events, including the 2024 Paris Olympics.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Natalie Stechyson has been a writer and editor at CBC News since 2021. She covers stories on social trends, families, gender, human interest, as well as general news. She's worked as a journalist since 2009, with stints at the Globe and Mail and Postmedia News, among others. Before joining CBC News, she was the parents editor at HuffPost Canada, where she won a silver Canadian Online Publishing Award for her work on pregnancy loss. You can reach her at natalie.stechyson@cbc.ca.
With files from CBC's Abby Hughes

articles.title: ICC prosecution says Duterte's detention 'necessary;' defense to seek review
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court"s (ICC) Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of former President Rodrigo Duterte, noting that it is “necessary”…
articles.byline: Andy Peñafuerte III, Jay-vee Marasigan Pangan

blocks.text: Published September 15, 2026 12:51am

The International Criminal Court’s (ICC) Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of former President Rodrigo Duterte, noting that it is “necessary” so he would not “interfere with witnesses.”

Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said “there has been no change” in Duterte’s circumstances that would prompt the Trial Chamber III to revise its previous order on the former president’s detention.

“To the contrary,” Niang noted in an observation filed on September 14, “there have been changes in circumstances that have increased the risk Mr. Duterte presents under articles 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) of the Statute.”

Niang was referring to the Rome Statute’s article on issuing a warrant of arrest, ensuring the appearance at a trial of a person facing charges, and that such person “does not obstruct or endanger the investigation or the court proceedings.”
Aside from a definitive trial date, Niang cited a redacted point, both of which he said “increase the likelihood of Mr Duterte facing trial and therefore increase the risk that he may abscond.”
Prosecution: Witnesses’ names disclosed to Duterte

“The Prosecution has also added ‘eight additional incidents’ to Mr Duterte’s charges since the date of the Decision,” Niang said, referring to the Trial Chamber's May 22, 2026 decision reviewing Duterte's detention. The prosecution cited its still-confidential pre-trial brief as the basis for the eight additional documents.
“The number of incidents and victims, and therefore the prospect of a lengthy prison sentence, have increased, which militates in favour of Mr Duterte’s continued detention.”
Niang also pointed out that the List of Witnesses that the Prosecution provided to Duterte on August 31, 2026 includes the “names of the Prosecution’s witnesses, as well as their expected testimony.”

“The question of the risks to witnesses ‘revolves around the possibility, not the inevitability, of a ‘future occurrence’. Mr Duterte’s history shows that he is able and has the means, either directly or through his associates, to interfere with [REDACTED].”
With these submissions, Niang argued, “Mr Duterte’s continued detention is necessary to ensure he does not interfere with witnesses.”
Defense: Fitness ruling should come first
Duterte’s lawyers, meanwhile, told the court that the question of his continued detention is linked to the still-pending determination of his fitness to stand trial.
“The questions of fitness and detention are necessarily linked,” Peter Haynes, Duterte’s defense counsel, said in an observation published on September 14.

In the filing, the defense said it had earlier informed the Chamber that it did not intend to submit observations on detention at that stage because it expected to return to the issue after the fitness question has been resolved.

“Following an order on 15 July 2026 from the Trial Chamber to submit observations pursuant to Rule 118(2),1 the Defence informed the Chamber, parties and participants on 4 September 2024 that ‘it does not intend to submit observations at this time’, but that it anticipated coming back as required after the question of the accused’s fitness to stand trial had been settled,” the statement read.
The defense raised concerns over Duterte’s fitness in May and requested that he undergo a medical examination.
Both sides have since made submissions on the experts’ reports, with the Prosecution asking Trial Chamber III to find Duterte fit to stand trial. The chamber’s decision is pending.

The Defense argued that if Duterte were found unfit to stand trial and the proceedings were consequently adjourned, then “this would be relevant to the assessment of whether there has been a material change in circumstances.”

The Defense said it intends to exercise Duterte’s right under Rule 118(2) to seek a review of the detention once the Trial Chamber has ruled on his fitness to stand trial, “if the circumstances merit it.”

The prosecution and defense filings were submitted as Trial Chamber III prepares for its latest review of Duterte’s detention, which is expected to be discussed at the third status conference on September 16, 2026. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 24: Ex-Sandiganbayan chief testifies on unexplained wealth
articles.summary: Retired Sandiganbayan Presiding Justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang took the witness stand on Day 24 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte to testify on what is considered unexplained,…

blocks.text: Retired Sandiganbayan Presiding Justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang took the witness stand on Day 24 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte to testify on what is considered unexplained, ill-gotten and hidden wealth of public officials and the respective consequences for these individuals.
Tang’s testimony before the Senate impeachment court, however, faced opposition from the defense, which argued that it could improperly touch on conclusions of law.

Tang’s testimony was still allowed because it only “takes judicial notice mandatorily of the laws but not what the law means in a specific or particular case,” including the impeachment case against the Vice President.
The retired justice later said that a public official’s acquisition of unexplained wealth as defined by the Civil Forfeiture Law is a ground for removal from post.

Likewise, she said that cash on hand and cash in bank of government officials must be separately declared in the Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), and must not be lumped together with other properties.
To recall, the absence of Duterte’s cash in bank on her SALN declarations from 2019 to 2024 was flagged during the House justice committee hearing on the impeachment complaints against her.

Duterte and her husband, Manases "Mans" Carpio reportedly had a total net worth of P55 million in 2019. It grew to P56 million in 2020; P65 million in 2021; P71 million in 2022; P77 million in 2023; P88 million in 2024, excluding cash on hand and deposits.

Michael Poa, spokesperson for the Vice President’s defense team, explained that Duterte had no cash on hand declared in her official SALN since 2019 because it was "lumped" under the “others” line item.
Businesses, spouses

Further, Tang testified that the President and Vice President are barred by the Constitution from participating in any business "given the fact that the President and Vice President are the two highest officials of the land, there is the greater possibility of abuse in their office.”

While she was mostly composed during her almost four hours of testimony, she became visibly stern when she responded to defense lawyer Mark Vinluan’s question asking if she was promised anything for testifying before the Senate impeachment court.
“No. My testimony is not for sale,” she replied. said.

The impeachment trial hearing took a lighter turn when Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian, a bachelor, was chided by his colleagues for asking Tang about why and how a public official should declare his or her spouse’s assets in their Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).
Senators Francis Escudero and Francis Pangilinan hinted that Gatchalian might also be preparing for marriage with such questions.

Tang, for her part, explained that under the Supreme Court’s ruling in Babano v. Executive Secretary, a public official must declare the assets of his or her spouse in the SALN unless the couple agreed to a complete separation of property before their marriage.

“In the case of Rabusa v. Republic [Supreme Court decision], his wife should be able to show she legitimately acquired those properties. Otherwise, if she fails to show that she has no financial capacity to acquire those assets and these assets are traceable to the public officials, that becomes the property of the public official, including businesses, provided that the ownership of those assets is traceable to the public official,” Tang said.

The defense panel took the opportunity to raise President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr.'s financial interests in some companies as reflected in his latest 2025 SALN, since Tang previously said that the President and Vice President are not allowed to participate in business interests as soon as they are elected to their respective posts.
Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano and Senator Pia Cayetano also raised concerns about supposed threats and intimidation against them.
Before the trial day ended, the Senate impeachment court ordered the Philippine National Bank and UnionBank to submit Vice President Sara Duterte's bank records by Thursday, September 17.

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said this is an extension of the initial timeframe the court provided, given the banks' request for more time to submit voluminous documents, and that the September 17 deadline is non-extendable.

Given Tang’s testimony, House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list said that House prosecution team is considering presenting documents on the 19 overseas trips of Vice President Sara Duterte from 2025 to 2026 as evidence to prove its allegation of her accumulated unexplained wealth.

As this developed, the House prosecution panel also said that the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte has failed in its efforts to sabotage the testimony Tang, who was able to testify on the following key points:
· a public official with proven unexplained wealth can be removed from office
· cash on hand and cash in bank should be declared under cash category of the SALN, not under “others”

· government authorities can scrutinize the wealth of the public official’s immediate family such as spouse and children, because this will prevent public officials from using their family members to hide their money
· laws require a public official to declare his or her spouse’s assets under his/her SALN unless they have a prenuptial agreement of separation of assets. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Immigrants held in small outdoor cages at 'Alligator Alcatraz' in Florida, investigators find
articles.summary: DHS inspectors say they found the immigration-detention centre violated basic standards for hygiene, medical care, food and safety.

blocks.text: In its response included in the investigation report, DHS officials said Florida - not the federal government - had authority over day-to-day operations at the facility.
The facility was established by the state of Florida through an executive order signed by DeSantis, but the federal government paid for operational costs.

In January, the OIG conducted a surprise inspection at the detention facility, which had become one of the most notorious immigration detention centres in the US. The OIG is an independent internal watchdog at DHS. The current inspector general was appointed by President Donald Trump during his first term.

In 2025, the detention facility was built over the course of eight days in the Everglades, a protected wetland known for its alligators. Trump once joked that immigrants held there would need to learn "how to run away" from the reptiles at the facility, which civil rights groups have decried as inhumane.
In June 2026, DeSantis said the facility would close as it was only meant to be temporary.

According to the OIG report, between July 2025 and January 2026, the facility kept 79 immigrants in the small metal enclosures, describing them as "calming areas" for people to "deescalate and have time alone". They were held there from periods ranging from minutes to nearly two hours, at least once as a disciplinary measure, OIG said.
"The use of such restrictive spaces is highly unconventional and does not align with standards for humane treatment," the report stated.

articles.title: Sweden’s political parties launch coalition talks as both blocs try to secure power
articles.summary:
Centre-left bloc led by Social Democrats has narrow lead with 95% of vote counted, but faces internal policy battle

Sweden’s political parties have launched coalition negotiations as the…

blocks.text: Sweden’s political parties have launched coalition negotiations as the Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson started the long and difficult process of trying to form a new government.

Full results from Sunday’s election are not expected until after overseas votes are counted on Wednesday, but with 95% of the votes counted, the Social Democrats and the centre-left bloc had a narrow but growing lead of 176 seats to the right-leaning parties’ 173.

After losing support for the first time since they were founded, the far-right Sweden Democrats, who were hoping to enter government for the first time, appear to be out of the picture. But many of their policy ideas – on immigration laws, integration and crime – have become mainstream, including in the centre-left.
Both Andersson and the outgoing centre-right prime minister, Ulf Kristersson, of the Moderates have each said they want to explore possible coalition options to secure power.

blocks.caption: Sweden's prime minister, Ulf Kristersson, leader of the conservative Moderates, has said he wants to explore possible coalitions to secure power for another term. Photograph: Christine Olsson/TT/TT News Agency/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: After a long election night during which there was just one seat between the two blocs, Social Democrat leaders met with Andersson on Monday morning at the party’s Stockholm headquarters.
Questions remain as to whether the bloc is willing to work with the Left party (Vänsterpartiet), which the Centre party has previously ruled out.

The Social Democrats press secretary, Tobias Baudin, said he had been in contact with colleagues from opposition parties and called for the resignation of Kristersson, who led the rightwing Tidö coalition government with the support of the Sweden Democrats.

“Now the voters have had their say and they have given him a failing grade for himself and his government,” Baudin told Swedish broadcaster SVT, adding: “He should resign himself. In fact it doesn’t matter, if he doesn’t resign he will be removed. How he does it is up to him.
The Centre party said that in talks with the Social Democrats it would be seeking a government with a “desire for political stability” and a “clear centre-right character” with no “fringe politics”.

Social Democrat Morgan Johansson, who under the last Social Democrat-led government was deputy prime minister, said the Centre party’s announcement was a positive development and that overall there were “good prospects”.
All of the left-leaning parties want a change of government, he said. “That is the starting point. I don’t think anyone wants us to end up in a situation where blockages lead to a new election.”
Meanwhile, Kristersson appears to be keeping his options open.
after newsletter promotion

On Sunday night he said the result could lead to a “complicated government formation, where it ends remains to be seen”. On Monday, ahead of a meeting with his fellow Tidö coalition leaders, he declined to elaborate, saying he would wait for a full result before having conversations. “If all the red lines remain then Sweden won’t have a government at all,” he added. “I plan to pursue a number of possibilities that may exist.”
The Liberals and the Christian Democrats have both said they will not work with the Social Democrats.
After the overseas votes are counted on Wednesday, the final election results are not expected to come until the weekend.

The new parliament will meet for the first time on 28 September and the earliest date that the speaker can suggest a prime minister is 29 September, but talks could take considerably longer. If, when parliament votes for a prime minister candidate, over half say no, then the speaker must find a new candidate. If there are four failed votes there will then automatically be a new election.
After the 2022 election, it took 37 days to form a government; in 2018, it took 134 days to form a new coalition.

Fredrik Furtenbach, the senior political correspondent at Sveriges Radio (Radio Sweden), said: “I think it will end with either the Left or Centre party having to give way. It might take several failed prime minister votes first.” But he does not believe that the Social Democrats and Moderates, who he describes as “traditional archenemies”, will end up working together. “You cannot share the position of prime minister.”

articles.title: British man accused of drugging and raping wife over two decades admits 60 offences
articles.summary:
Man, who cannot be named to protect anonymity of his victim, admits scores of criminal offences

A man has pleaded guilty to drugging and sexually assaulting his wife over a period of 20…

blocks.text: A man has pleaded guilty to drugging and sexually assaulting his wife over a period of 20 years as he admitted 60 criminal offences.
The man, who cannot be named in order to protect the anonymity of his victim, is in his 60s and before his arrest lived in Stockport, Greater Manchester.
He admitted 60 counts, which include 21 counts of rape and sharing intimate images of his victim.
His estranged wife sat on the front row of the packed courtroom with other family members as he entered his pleas, occasionally sobbing as he did so.
In June, the man pleaded guilty to 15 of the charges against him. On Monday he admitted the final 45 at Manchester’s Minshull Street crown court.

articles.title: Africa's richest man launches continent's biggest share sale
articles.summary: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote says he wants ordinary people to share in the success of his oil refinery.

blocks.text: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote has launched Africa's largest ever share sale, offering a stake in his oil refinery to the general public in a deal that could raise as much as $2.1bn (£1.6bn).
The initial public offering (IPO) is for roughly 3% of the Dangote refinery, with the billionaire saying he wanted to give ordinary Nigerians the chance to share in the plant's success.
The refinery, which started production in 2024, is one of the largest in the world and took more than a decade to complete.
It now supplies more than 70% of Nigeria's energy consumption, and many Nigerians have expressed excitement at the prospect of owning a part of it.
Among them is Isah Salisu, who told the BBC he withdrew 50,000 naira (£28; $37) from his savings to invest.
"My hope is that my small money will one day grow big. I don't want to miss out as many I know are also investing," he said.
The IPO lasts for a month and the minimum purchase is 10 shares, costing about $4.
Economy and business expert Dr Abdulrazak Ibrahim Fagge told the BBC that Monday's event was historic.
But he warned investors that the price of the shares could fall, meaning people could lose some of their money.
"What prospective buyers, especially first-time buyers, should know is that they shouldn't invest all their money or money they would need in a couple of months," he said.
"They should invest something they could do without for the next three, four, five years."
He also warned people to be wary of scammers, saying there are people who would want to take advantage of those without good knowledge of the process.
"I will advise people to only deal with the institutions that have been listed," he said.
Nigeria is Africa's biggest oil producer but until the refinery was opened, most of the country's fuel had to be imported because of a lack of refining capacity in the country.
Born in Kano, Dangote, 67, has a net worth of around $28bn, according to Forbes magazine.
He made his fortune in cement and sugar in Nigeria before expanding to 16 other African countries.
His company Dangote Cement is Africa's largest cement producer.
The Lagos refinery was first announced in 2013 with an initial estimated cost of around $19bn, but construction did not begin until 2017. It was further delayed by the Covid-19 pandemic.
The site, in the Lekki Free Zone near Lagos, required massive land reclamation, with 65 million cubic metres of sand moved.
The refinery has a processing capacity of 650,000 barrels per day, making it the seventh-largest in the world.
The money raised by the share offer is intended to help double its capacity.

articles.title: UK armed forces member killed in crash in Ukraine
articles.summary:
Ministry of Defence says person died in road incident understood not to be result of hostile action

A member of the UK armed forces has been killed in a crash in Ukraine, the Ministry of…

blocks.text: A member of the UK armed forces has been killed in a crash in Ukraine, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) said.
The MoD said the person died in a road traffic incident on Saturday.
It is understood the incident was not as a result of hostile action.
Their family has been informed and has asked for some time before more details are released.
“Our thoughts and our sympathies are with the individual’s loved ones at this difficult time,” an MoD spokesperson said.
The defence secretary, Wes Streeting, said on X: “This is very sad news for the family and for those grieving with them in our Armed Forces.
“My deepest condolences go to them all.”
There is a small number of British personnel in Ukraine who provide security to diplomats and support the country’s armed forces.
British paratrooper George Hooley, 28, was killed in Ukraine in December when he watched Ukrainian forces testing a new defensive capability.
The MoD described his death as a “tragic accident”.
Russia’s full scale invasion of Ukraine is in its fifth year and the conflict continues with fresh strikes on Ukraine including at a gas works and a drone attack on a station on Sunday.
The attack hit a train at Yahodyn station, on the Polish border, shortly after a train carrying Boris Johnson had left ahead of schedule.
Ukraine’s railway operator said the attack may have been aimed at the train carrying the former prime minister, among other dignitaries.
Johnson had been returning from a major conference in Kyiv along with former Swedish prime minister Carl Bildt and a number of European security advisers.
According to a translation from Ukrainian, rail operator Ukrzaliznytsia said in a post on Telegram it was “quite possible” the drone had been aimed at Johnson’s train.

items: Mansor Ebrahim of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party won the 1st District seat in the Special Geographic Area, defeating Butch Malang of the Bangsamoro Federalist Party.
Ebrahim's victory allows him to serve a special five-year transition term in the Bangsamoro Parliament.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The highly contested head-to-head race between the son of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) chairman and the high-ranking officer stripped of a position has finally concluded.

In the end, it was the MILF’s United Bangsamoro Justice Party that prevailed. The UBJP’s Mansor Ebrahim, the son of MILF Chairman Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim, topped the race for the 1st District seat of the Special Geographic Area (SGA).
He received 29,061 votes, according to 100% of the SGA’s election returns for the 2026 Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao parliamentary elections as of Monday, September 14, 11:29 pm.

The Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), the UBJP’s rival, fielded Butch Malang, who is the former SGA Development Authority administrator, a member of the region’s interim parliament, and the recently axed chair of the MILF Coordinating Committee on the Cessation of Hostilities.
Malang only got 17,386 votes.
The stakes were particularly high in this race because of Malang’s history with the MILF.

Just a week before the election, it was the central committee led by the Ebrahim patriarch that stripped Malang of his committee chairmanship. A news release by the MILF’s information committee owed it to “a leadership rift years in the making.”

It apparently began when President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. unceremoniously replaced the elder Ebrahim as interim chief minister with then-MILF army chief Abdulraof Macacua in March 2025. (READ: MILF central committee frowns on BARMM leadership change)

Tensions only grew as Macacua began making decisions as chief minister without consulting the MILF. In the end, Macacua and several other high-ranking MILF officials, including Malang, defected from the UBJP to the BFP.

Macacua, Malang, and their cohorts had been suspended from their positions in the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces for months before they were eventually removed — though they remain members of the MILF.

With Malang defeated, the younger Ebrahim is set to serve a special five-year transition term from October 30, 2026, to June 30, 2031. He will be one of the 32 district representatives making up 40% of the 80-seat Bangsamoro Parliament. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Defense questions ex-Sandigan presiding justice as witness
articles.summary: The defense panel has questioned the decision of the prosecution to present retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang as the Senate impeachment court tackles the article on the…

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
Retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang appears before the Senate impeachment court on September 14, 2026.
SPPA

MANILA, Philippines — The defense panel has questioned the decision of the prosecution to present retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang as the Senate impeachment court tackles the article on the alleged unexplained wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte.
In a manifestation, defense lawyer Mark Vinluan said the presentation of Cabotaje-Tang is improper.

“This is the first time that the Vice President is being confronted with Justice Tang and her testimony. For the record, she is not listed in the pre-trial order as a witness and there is no reservation for a witness with her designation or background,” said Vinluan.
“So, for all intents and purposes, Justice Tang is a surprise witness, which violates fair play and is prohibited under the rules,” Vinluan said.
“In light of the foregoing, we will move for the exclusion of the testimony of Justice Tang and will submit to this Court’s discretion as to the presentation of her testimony,” Vinluan said.

He added that the prosecution did not even furnish the defense with copies beforehand, saying that this is already the third time that the prosecution has attempted to present a witness without first furnishing the defense with the materials to be used.
“We don’t know her personal background, and we don’t know the extent of her testimony and the documents that she will identify, if any,” Vinluan noted.
According to Vinluan, the notice on Sept. 9 was only to Cabotaje-Tang’s name, previous official function and general purpose of her testimony.
He said it is the position of the defense that the presentation of Cabotaje-Tang infringes on the Vice President’s right to intelligently cross-examine her.

“And more importantly, (it) violates the Vice President’s constitutional right to due process, particularly her right to be promptly and completely informed of the nature and cause of the accusation against her,” he added.
Vinluan noted that in the Philippines, being a legal expert is not an official designation and is quite subjective.
“We don’t know the extent of her legal knowledge, her political background, whether she’s neutral, DDS, loyalista or kakampink, which is hardly distinguishable nowadays,” he noted.
Presumption of innocence
The defense maintained that the Vice President enjoys presumption of innocence as the prosecution is “hellbent” on removing her from office.
During cross-examination of Cabotaje-Tang, Vinluan stressed that it is not the prosecution’s primary duty to convict.
“The prosecution should not be too eager to convict. Vice President Sara enjoys the presumption of innocence, correct?” Vinluan said.
He said that if the prosecution fails “to discharge this burden,” Duterte is entitled to an acquittal.
“At any rate, conviction must be based on the strength of the prosecution and not the weakness of the defense,” Vinluan added.
Cabotaje-Tang agreed with Vinluan but based on the point of view of criminal lawyers.
Oral arguments
The defense is ready for the oral arguments on the two-thirds threshold to convict the Vice President.
Defense spokesman Michael Poa said they have decided who will represent Duterte during the oral arguments but will not disclose the name.

Impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol said the Senate impeachment court will need 11 votes from the active roster of 20 senators to overturn the ruling setting the conviction threshold at 16 votes in Duterte’s impeachment trial. — Marc Jayson Cayabyab

articles.title: 64% say district reps ‘doing a good job’ – OCTA
articles.summary: About six in every 10 Filipinos believe that their district representatives are doing a good job, indicating what the OCTA Research group described as a stark difference between views at the local…

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. delivered his fifth State of the Nation Address at plenary hall of the House of Representatives in Quezon City, July 27, 2026.
Philippine STAR / Noel B. Pabalate

MANILA, Philippines — About six in every 10 Filipinos believe that their district representatives are doing a good job, indicating what the OCTA Research group described as a stark difference between views at the local and institutional levels.
In its July 4 to 11 survey, OCTA found 64 percent of the respondents agreed their current district representatives were doing a good job. Only 27 percent disagreed, while nine percent were undecided.
This is far higher than the 38 percent trust and 37 percent performance rating obtained by the House of Representatives as an institution.

“The finding that local representative satisfaction substantially exceeds institutional trust and institutional performance ratings suggests that accountability in Philippine politics may operate more effectively, or at least more visibly, at the constituency level than at the level of the institution itself,” OCTA said.

“This has implications beyond public opinion measurement: it bears on how legislators themselves may calculate political incentives, since a representative’s standing with constituents appears largely decoupled from the public’s broader assessment of Congress,” it added.

The survey firm said it may also offer partial explanation for a familiar pattern in Philippine electoral behavior showing high incumbent reelection rates despite low institutional trust in Congress as a whole.
OCTA pointed out how regional variation in satisfaction with district representation “is not a uniform national mood, but a locally contingent one.”

articles.title: Economy ‘more than steady’ – Marcos
articles.summary: Despite inflation concerns and the weakening of the peso, President Marcos described the Philippines as “more than steady.”

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Malacañang on February 23, 2026.
PPA pool photos by Niño Jesus Orbeta
MANILA, Philippines — Despite inflation concerns and the weakening of the peso, President Marcos described the Philippines as “more than steady.”

Speaking to reporters in New Delhi on Sunday, Marcos attributed the weakness of the peso and higher unemployment partly to inflation and reduced public spending following the flood control corruption scandal.

“The peso to the dollar, it’s because of inflation, because of all the weaknesses that we are seeing. Unemployment went up. And that’s, again, because of lack of public spending. That’s the effect there. So at least it’s something that we can do something about and are doing something about,” Marcos said.

He declined to make promises about inflation, citing high oil prices and the continuing Middle East conflict, but said economic improvements should become visible as government spending increases and more jobs are created.
Inflation eased to 6.1 percent in August from 6.2 percent in July as food prices rose at a slower pace.
However, average inflation for the first eight months reached 5.2 percent, well above the government’s full-year target of three percent.

Unemployment also climbed to six percent in July from 4.9 percent in June and 5.3 percent a year earlier, translating to 3.14 million jobless Filipinos. It was the highest unemployment rate since June 2022, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority.

To address this, the President said the administration was expanding assistance programs to cushion vulnerable sectors from the impact of the Middle East crisis, including subsidies for farmers and scholarships.

“The UPLIFT program is having a good effect, we see in the stats that those that are being reached by these programs are widening in terms of who gets assistance from the government as the... systems of assistance become more established,” he said.
National government outstanding debt reached P19.39 trillion at the end of July.

Marcos made the remarks before returning to Manila early Monday after a two-day working visit to New Delhi, where he represented the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations at the 18th BRICS Summit. — Helen Flores
